rounds.text: Alivus Life Sciences demonstrates superior capital efficiency, evidenced by an ROE of 17.9% [E13] and an ROCE of 23.8% [E12], both of which significantly outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. This operational excellence is further validated by a robust 25% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E19] and a strong cash conversion ratio of 1.00x, ensuring that reported profits are fully backed by actual cash flow [E30]. The company is aggressively reinvesting in its future, as shown by a 178.4% surge in capital work-in-progress [E35] and a planned FY27 capex of INR 540 crores, all funded through internal accruals [E86]. Institutional confidence is rising, reflected in the positive money flow [E39] and increased holdings by both foreign and domestic institutions since late 2023 [E37, E38]. Conceded: the company faces a negative margin of safety based on DCF analysis [E40, E41], a decline in promoter holdings [E36], and high debtor days of 153 [E57]. Despite these challenges, the company’s ability to maintain a debt-free balance sheet [E85] while scaling its high-potent API portfolio—which targets a massive $82 billion addressable market—positions it for sustained long-term value creation [E82].

Conceded: the company demonstrates high returns on capital and equity [E12, E13], alongside full cash conversion on Mar 2026 profits [E30]. However, the bull's focus on short-term profit metrics obscures a persistently sluggish top-line growth record of only 6% compounded over both three and five years [E14, E15], falling well below sector median sales growth of 17.5% [E67]. Furthermore, the aggressive reinvestment and surge in capital work-in-progress of 178.4% [E35] carry execution and capital allocation hazards, particularly when paired with a severe working capital drag of 153 high debtor days [E57]. While institutional holdings increased overall [E37, E38], this accumulation occurred alongside a notable 8.00 percentage point reduction in promoter ownership from Dec 2023 to Sep 2026 [E36]. Finally, the reliance on internal accruals for a massive INR 540 crore capex program in FY27 [E86] takes place against a backdrop of a muted and inventory-rationalized GPL segment that suffered a 52.6% year-on-year decline in Q1 [E87], exposing the growth narrative to severe concentration and demand vulnerabilities.

evidence.fact: Management expects revenue growth of 10% to 12% in FY27.
